question: Which two items did Max say are the biggest cost drivers in his rough estimate for upgrading the pressure rating on the Transwestern mainline?

steps.text: Plan: find Max's email on the Transwestern mainline pressure rating upgrade estimate, then identify the two biggest cost drivers he named, and confirm by reading the email.

steps.arguments: {"query": "Max rough estimate upgrade pressure rating Transwestern mainline biggest cost drivers"}
steps.summary: 10 results, 10 of them people's own mail

answer:
Max Brown's 2001-05-15 email names the two biggest cost drivers, and the search result shows the full text, so I didn't need to open it separately.

In his rough estimate for a possible Transwestern MAOP upgrade, replacement of the mainline valves and replacement costs for the Class 3 pipe are the highest drivers. The estimate covers the 30" mainline and loop lines from Station 5 to the Colorado River.

Max called the estimate very rough. He said he was still waiting on information from Facility Planning. He also said that if there are other alternatives later defined in lieu of pipe replacement for class 3 pipe, this would also drive this cost down.

citations.cited_text: As can be seen, replacement of the mainline valves and replacement costs for the Class 3 pipe are the highest drivers.  We are still uncertain whether the valves on the launchers and receivers are rated for 1008 psig and have not been included at this time for replacement.  I will check on this while in the Gallup area.  All of the valves requiring replacment will have some salvage and reuse value for potential use on other pipeline systems in ETS that will need to be converted to being smart piggable in the future I am quite sure.  If there are other alternatives later defined in lieu of pipe replacment for class 3 pipe, this would also drive this cost down.
